leftEvidence.title: Apostolic witness is traced from John’s baptism

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Peter requires a replacement witness who accompanied the group from John’s baptism until Jesus’ ascension.
points.right: Peter summarizes the word proclaimed through Judea beginning from Galilee after John’s baptism.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The selected person must become a witness of the resurrection.
points.right: He says God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power, then moves through deeds, death, resurrection, witnesses, and forgiveness.

payload.posture: Acts uses John’s baptism both to qualify a witness and to locate the beginning of Jesus’ public story.

rightEvidence.title: Peter begins Jesus’ public story after John’s baptism

payload.tension: One passage defines continuous presence; the other gives a theological-historical summary.
payload.title: From John’s baptism to apostolic witness
